Package frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve

Class SwerveController

java.lang.Object
frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveController
public class SwerveController extends Object
The recommended front door for driving the swerve: layers rotation-to-angle PID (lookAt(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d)), point-to-point translation PID (pidTo(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d)), and a named-channel gate (setControl(frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveSpeeds, java.lang.String)/setChannel(java.lang.String)) on top of the raw Swerve drivetrain, so only whichever command currently "owns" the requested channel can actually move the robot.

  • Constructor Details

    • SwerveController

      public SwerveController(SwerveControllerConstants constants)
      Builds the rotation PID (profiled if cruiseVelocity/acceleration are set in SwerveControllerConstants.rotationPIDConstants, otherwise a plain continuous-input PID) and the drive PID from constants. Disabled if SwerveControllerConstants.swerveConstants is null.
      Parameters:
      constants - the rotation/drive PID gains and underlying swerve configuration

  • Method Details

    • setInstance

      public static void setInstance(SwerveController swerveController)
      Sets the singleton instance returned by get(). Call once during robot init.

    • get

      public static SwerveController get()
      Returns:
      the singleton SwerveController instance set via setInstance(frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveController), or a disabled no-op instance (logging a warning) if none has been set yet

    • lookAt

      public double lookAt(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d angle)
      PID-calculates the rotational velocity (rad/s) needed to turn the robot to face angle. Does not drive the swerve; feed the result into Swerve.drive(frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveSpeeds).
      Parameters:
      angle - the field-relative angle to face
      Returns:
      rotational velocity in radians/second, or 0 if disabled

    • lookAt

      public double lookAt(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d direction)
      Same as lookAt(Rotation2d), but takes a direction vector instead of an angle. The zero vector has no defined angle, so it's treated as "no target" and returns 0.
      Parameters:
      direction - the field-relative direction to face
      Returns:
      rotational velocity in radians/second, or 0 if disabled or direction is zero

    • lookAt

      public double lookAt(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d target, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d offset)
      Same as lookAt(Rotation2d), but faces a field-relative target pose (e.g. a goal), skewed by offset to aim a mechanism that isn't robot-front-facing.
      Parameters:
      target - the field-relative pose to look at
      offset - extra rotation applied to the look-at direction before aiming
      Returns:
      rotational velocity in radians/second, or 0 if disabled

    • resetLookAt

      public void resetLookAt()
      Resets the profiled rotation PID's state to the robot's current heading, so the next lookAt(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d) call doesn't use a stale setpoint/velocity from a previous target. Only meaningful when the profiled rotation PID is in use; otherwise logs and does nothing, since a plain PIDController has no motion-profile state to reset.

    • pidTo

      public edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d pidTo(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d target)
      PID-calculates a velocity vector, in m/s, that drives the robot straight towards target. Does not drive the swerve; feed the result into Swerve.drive(frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveSpeeds).
      Parameters:
      target - the field-relative point to drive towards
      Returns:
      a velocity vector pointing at target, or the zero vector if disabled

    • setControl

      public void setControl(SwerveSpeeds input, String channel)
      Drives the swerve with input, but only if channel matches the currently active channel (see setChannel(java.lang.String)). This is the gate that lets multiple commands share the drivetrain safely: a command that isn't the current channel owner silently has no effect.
      Parameters:
      input - the speeds to drive with if this call is authorized
      channel - the channel the caller believes it owns

    • setChannel

      public void setChannel(String channel)
      Switches which channel is allowed to drive the swerve via setControl(frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveSpeeds, java.lang.String), remembering the old one in getPreviousChannel().
      Parameters:
      channel - the channel to make active
